slides.title: Message, Media, and Device-Based Vectors
points: Threat vectors are the paths attackers use to reach users or systems. Objective 2.2 includes message-based attacks, image/file-based delivery, voice calls, removable media, and vulnerable software.
Security+ Objective 2.2: explain common threat vectors and attack surfaces.

slides.title: Email
slides.teach: Email can deliver malicious links, attachments, credential-harvesting pages, or fraudulent requests.

course.learn: Email can deliver malicious links, attachments, credential-harvesting pages, or fraudulent requests.

breakdown.explanation: The attacker uses email as the delivery path.
Malicious attachment, Credential phishing link, Spoofed sender

course.why: Email is widely trusted and commonly used, making it an effective vector for malware and social engineering.
course.example: A user receives a fake password-reset email linking to a credential-harvesting site.
course.check_q: Which vector uses email messages to deliver a malicious link or attachment?

slides.title: Short Message Service (SMS)
slides.teach: SMS can deliver malicious links or fraudulent requests to mobile users.

course.learn: SMS can deliver malicious links or fraudulent requests to mobile users.

breakdown.explanation: The attacker uses text messages as the delivery path.
Fake delivery text, Bank alert scam

course.why: Users often trust urgent mobile messages and may click links quickly.
course.example: A fake package-delivery text links to a malicious login page.
course.exam: Text message → SMS / SMISHING if social engineering.
course.check_q: Which message-based vector uses mobile text messages?

slides.title: Instant Messaging (IM)
slides.teach: Chat platforms can be used to send malicious links, files, or impersonation attempts.

course.learn: Chat platforms can be used to send malicious links, files, or impersonation attempts.

breakdown.explanation: The attacker uses a chat or messaging app.
Malicious Teams/Slack link, Compromised chat account

course.why: Business chat tools can feel more trusted and immediate than email.
course.example: A compromised chat account sends a malicious file to coworkers.
course.check_q: Which vector uses business chat platforms?

slides.title: Image-based
slides.teach: Images can carry malicious content, hidden data, QR-code lures, or exploit malformed image processing.

course.learn: Images can carry malicious content, hidden data, QR-code lures, or exploit malformed image processing.

breakdown.explanation: The image itself or something embedded in it is the delivery mechanism.
Malicious QR code, Crafted image file

course.why: Visual content may bypass user suspicion or direct users to malicious destinations.
course.example: A QR code in a flyer redirects users to a credential-stealing site.
course.exam: QR code or crafted image → IMAGE-BASED.
course.check_q: Which vector best describes a malicious QR code?

slides.title: File-based
slides.teach: Files may contain malware, malicious macros, scripts, or exploit code.

course.learn: Files may contain malware, malicious macros, scripts, or exploit code.

breakdown.explanation: The payload arrives as a file.
Malicious Office file, PDF exploit, Executable attachment

course.why: Users may open trusted-looking documents that execute harmful content.
course.example: A spreadsheet attachment contains a malicious macro.
course.check_q: Which vector delivers malware through a document or executable?

slides.title: Voice Call
slides.teach: Attackers can use phone calls to manipulate victims into revealing information or taking unsafe actions.

course.learn: Attackers can use phone calls to manipulate victims into revealing information or taking unsafe actions.

breakdown.explanation: The attacker uses a live or recorded phone conversation.
Fake help desk call, Fraudulent bank call

course.why: Voice interaction can create urgency and trust.
course.example: A caller pretends to be IT and asks for the user's MFA code.
course.exam: Phone call → VOICE CALL / VISHING when phishing by voice.
course.check_q: Which vector uses a phone conversation?

slides.title: Removable Device
slides.teach: USB drives and other removable media can introduce malware or enable unauthorized data transfer.

course.learn: USB drives and other removable media can introduce malware or enable unauthorized data transfer.
course.why: Removable media can bypass network defenses and move code or data physically.
course.example: An employee finds a USB drive in the parking lot and plugs it into a workstation.
course.check_q: Which vector involves infected USB media?

slides.title: Vulnerable Software
slides.teach: Software flaws can create an attack surface that attackers exploit.

course.learn: Software flaws can create an attack surface that attackers exploit.

breakdown.explanation: The attacker abuses a security weakness in software.

course.why: Known or unknown software vulnerabilities can allow code execution, privilege escalation, or access.
course.example: An attacker exploits an unpatched browser vulnerability.
course.check_q: Which vector relies on exploiting a software weakness?

slides.title: Client-based vs. Agentless
slides.teach: Client-based approaches rely on software installed on endpoints; agentless approaches operate without a persistent local agent.

course.learn: Client-based approaches rely on software installed on endpoints; agentless approaches operate without a persistent local agent.

breakdown.explanation: Ask whether software must be installed locally on the endpoint.
Endpoint security agent, Remote agentless scanning

course.why: The distinction affects deployment, visibility, compatibility, and how systems are monitored or assessed.
course.example: A vulnerability scanner assesses a server remotely without installing persistent local software.
course.exam: Installed local software = client-based; no persistent local agent = agentless.
course.check_q: What distinguishes client-based from agentless approaches?
course.check_a: Whether a persistent local agent/software is installed.

blocks.title: Message, Media, and Device-Based Vectors comparison
Identify the delivery path
items: The delivery path is a communication platform.
Example: A fake password-reset link arrives by SMS.
The lure or malicious content is delivered through an image.
Example: A QR code redirects the victim to a credential-harvesting site.
The malicious payload is delivered as a file.
Example: A spreadsheet contains a malicious macro.
The attacker uses a live or recorded call.
Example: A caller pretends to be IT support.
USB or external media → REMOVABLE DEVICE
Example: An infected USB is inserted into a workstation.
Exploit an unpatched flaw → VULNERABLE SOFTWARE
The attack succeeds because software contains an exploitable weakness.
Example: An attacker compromises an outdated browser.
blocks.example: Memory: Message · Image · File · Voice · USB · Vulnerability.

questions.q: A user receives a fake password-reset message by email that links to a credential-harvesting site. Which threat vector is being used?
questions.explanation: The malicious content is delivered through email.

questions.q: A fake package-delivery text message contains a malicious link. Which message-based vector is this?
questions.explanation: The delivery path is an SMS text message.

questions.q: A compromised business chat account sends malicious links to coworkers. Which vector is being used?
questions.explanation: The malicious content is delivered through a chat platform.

questions.q: A QR code redirects users to a fake login site. Which threat vector best fits?
questions.explanation: The attack is delivered through visual/image content.

questions.q: A spreadsheet attachment contains a malicious macro. Which threat vector best fits?
questions.explanation: The malicious payload is delivered in a file.

questions.q: A caller pretending to be IT asks a user for an MFA code. Which vector is being used?
questions.explanation: The attack uses a phone conversation.

questions.q: An employee plugs in an infected USB drive and malware executes. Which vector is most relevant?
questions.explanation: The malware is introduced through removable media.

questions.q: An attacker compromises a workstation by exploiting an unpatched browser flaw. Which vector is most relevant?
questions.explanation: The attacker exploits a software vulnerability.

questions.q: A scanner evaluates a server remotely without installing persistent software on the server. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Agentless approaches operate without a persistent local agent.
